To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a thermochemical pretreatement based on sodium hydroxyde addition is able to enhance the anaerobic biogasification of an industrial microbial sludge, but the improvement is limited due to the formation of inhibitory and/or non biodegradable molecules.

the thermochemical pretreatments of an industrial microbial sludge can enhance its anaerobic biogas production, provided that the soluble compounds formed during the pretreatment are not inhibitory or recalcitrant.

the thermochemical pretreatments of a microbial biomass, which is the main component of the solid fraction of the organic fraction of municipal solid wastes, enhance COD solubility but do not enhance anaerobic biogas production.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the anaerobic biotreatments of solid wastes and the improvement of the biodegradability through the use of physicochemical pretreatments.
the study of the influence of a thermochemical pretreatments on the biotoxicity and anaerobic biorefining performances of the pretreated microbial biomass.
the improvement of anaerobic digestion processes by thermochemical pretreatment, but also with the understanding of the physicochemical phenomena involved in the pretreatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thermochemical pretreatments, even when they are optimized, are not able to improve the anaerobic biotransformation of the pretreated microbial biomass.
the thermochemical pretreated biomass was not more anaerobically degradable but the biogas production was improved due to the removal of high molecular weight compounds.

thermochemical treatment can improve the anaerobic biogas potential of an industrial microbial sludge, but only when the soluble compounds generated during the treatment are not biotoxic or biorefractory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of thermochemical pretreatment is a good strategy to increase the solubilization and the biodegradability, but the biotoxicity of the soluble fraction of the pretreated biomass is a limiting factor.

the use of thermochemical pretreatment is a good strategy to enhance anaerobic biogas production, provided that a proper control of the pretreatment is applied in order to minimize the formation of high molecular weight compounds.

the thermochemical pretreatments are efficient for solubilization, but the biotoxicity of soluble compounds generated during pretreatments should be taken into account in order to optimize anaerobic digestion.
The main takeaway from our work is that

thermochemical pretreatment can be used to enhance anaerobic biogasification, but that the pretreated substrate must be fractioned to eliminate the high molecular weight compounds responsible for the poor biodegradation and the inhibition of microorganisms.
the thermochemical pretreatments are not sufficient to improve the anaerobic biogas potential of solid wastes.

thermochemical pretreatment is not sufficient to promote anaerobic digestion, but it can be used as an efficient way to improve the biogas production from the microbial biomass by removing the high molecular weight compounds responsible for poor biodegradabilty and toxicity to the microorganisms.
